info.title: Roezan Integrations API
info.description: Roezan Public API for Third-Party Integration

post.description:
By passing in phone & message body, you can trigger an SMS or MMS send on behalf of the authenticated account, from another service. Maximum of 10 media links to include, max message size of 5MB including text and media. Images may not exceed 5MB and all other media may not exceed 600KB.

If your account has more than one number, pass `from` to choose which one sends. See `from` below and `GET /api/integrations/senders`.

**Idempotency:** send an optional `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe. A retry with the same key replays the first response instead of sending a second message.

400.description: Unexpected error while queueing the message

409.description: A request with this Idempotency-Key is already being processed

422.description: The request cannot be acted on: `phone` is missing, none of `message` / `media` / `mediaUrl` was supplied, `from` was rejected, or the `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a different request. `from` and idempotency rejections carry a `code`.

get.description:
Returns the phone numbers on your account that `from` can name when sending a message. Each `id` is the same `id` that appears in webhook payloads (`sender` on `message.status`, `recipient` on `message.receive`).

Released numbers are not listed. A number that cannot send yet — for example a toll-free number awaiting verification — is listed with `canSend: false` and a `reason`.

OAuth tokens and scoped keys need the `account:read` scope.

get.summary: Gets all List objects for your account
get.description: Fetches all of your Lists which is useful for Subscribe-to-List and Unsubscribe-from-list API calls, where the ID of the List is required

get.summary: Gets all custom Fields for your account
get.description: Fetches all of your custom fields defined in your Roezan account, to be listed as options to specify and set on a given contact. Key 'type' can be one of 'string', 'number', 'datetime', 'boolean'

get.summary: Gets all Tag objects for your account
get.description: Fetches all of your Tags which is useful for Add-Contact-Tag and Remove-Contact-Tag API calls, where the ID of the Tag is required

post.summary: Creates/Subscribes a Contact to a List
post.description: By specifying Contact details and a List ID, you can create new contacts if applicable and subscribe them to the specified List. List IDs can be found in the Admin dashboard Lists page

put.summary: Unsubscribes a Contact from a List
put.description: Unsubscribes the Contact matching the given phone number from the specified List. List IDs can be found in the Admin dashboard Lists page.

requestBody.description: Contact phone number and the List to unsubscribe from

post.description: Creates a new Contact or updates an existing Contact, including related tags and subscribed lists

202.description: Contact created; tags, fields and lists are applied asynchronously

400.description: Unexpected error while creating the contact

get.summary: Fetch a contact by phone or email
get.description: Fetches a single contact by phone number or email address. Provide at least one of `phone` or `email` as a query parameter. When both are supplied, `phone` is matched first and `email` is used as a fallback. Internal-only fields (opt-out reason, message-state, location source) are stripped from the response.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: Contact phone number. Accepts common formats; normalized server-side (e.g. `17276560957`). Required if `email` is omitted.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Contact email address. Used as a fallback when `phone` is omitted or yields no match. Required if `phone` is omitted.

422.description: Neither phone nor email was supplied

post.summary: Adds a Tag to a Contact
post.description: Send Contact information for a new or existing Contact, with Phone being required, along with a list of Tag IDs to apply the Tags to a new or existing Contact

requestBody.description: Contact info (Phone at least) and array of Tag IDs to apply to the Contact

delete.summary: Removes a Tag from a Contact
delete.description: Specify a Tag ID and Contact Phone number to remove the given Tag from the Contact if they exist

requestBody.description: Contact info (Phone at least) and Tag ID to remove from the Contact

422.description: phone or tagId is missing, or tagId is not a number

get.description:
Returns a contact's message history (including broadcasts) by Roezan contact ID, newest-first.

**Pagination** is keyset/cursor-based: follow `next_cursor` (pass it back as `cursor`) until `has_more` is `false`. Treat `next_cursor` as opaque — do not build or parse it. When following a cursor, keep the filter params (`source`, `direction`, `createdAtFrom`/`createdAtTo`) identical across pages; changing them mid-walk yields inconsistent results.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests/second per credential (in addition to the global integrations limit). Exceeding it returns `429` with `RateLimit-*` headers.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque token from a prior response's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: createdAtFrom
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be paired with `createdAtTo`.

parameters.name: createdAtTo
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be paired with `createdAtFrom`.

400.description: Invalid contact id, source, date range, or cursor

404.description: Contact not found (or not in this account)

get.description:
Returns the list of Roezan contact IDs a broadcast was actually sent to (the historical sent-set captured at send time), ascending by contact ID.

**Pagination** is keyset/cursor-based: follow `next_cursor` (pass it back as `cursor`) until `has_more` is `false`. Treat `next_cursor` as opaque — do not build or parse it.

**Retention:** recipients are retained for approximately 90 days. A broadcast older than the retention window (or one created before this feature launched) returns an empty `recipients` array with `has_more: false`.

**Rate limit:** 5 requests/second per credential (in addition to the global integrations limit). Exceeding it returns `429` with `RateLimit-*` headers.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque token from a prior response's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page.

404.description: Broadcast not found (or not in this account)

post.description:
Creates a **draft** broadcast targeting one or more of the account's lists and returns the saved draft together with the expected recipient count and a credit estimate. This is step one of a two-step flow: **nothing is sent until you call `POST /api/integrations/broadcasts/{id}/schedule`**.

**Targeting (v1):** lists only, via `list_ids`. The caller is expected to already know its list IDs (see `GET /api/integrations/lists`). Segment and event targeting are not supported yet; sending `segment_id`/`event_ids` returns `422` rather than being silently ignored.

**`message` is required** — unlike `POST /api/integrations/message/send`, a broadcast cannot be media-only.

**`scheduled_time` (optional) is stored as intent, not scheduled here.** If provided it is validated now (Eastern default when `scheduled_timezone` is omitted; an explicit offset/`Z` in the value wins over `scheduled_timezone`; past-by-more-than-60s and more-than-366-days-out are rejected `422`; DST-ambiguous local times resolve to the nearest valid instant). At `/schedule` you may confirm it as-is, override it with a fresh `scheduled_time`, or ignore it with `send_now: true` to send immediately. A draft created with no `scheduled_time` cannot be bare-confirmed: `/schedule` rejects it `422` (`send_time_required`) unless the call says when.

**Estimate (warn-only here):** the message becomes **MMS** when it spans three or more segments or includes media; MMS is billed at three segments per recipient. `estimated_credits = recipients × segments_per_message`. The recipient count is de-duplicated across lists and excludes contacts unsubscribed from the list, opted out, invalid, or deleted (actual sends can be lower). `estimate.within_budget` is `false` when the projected usage would exceed the account's remaining credit budget — the draft is still created; the budget is **enforced at `/schedule`**.

**Rate limit:** 1 request/second per credential (in addition to the global integrations limit).

**Idempotency:** send an optional `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe (see the header docs).

**Field aliases:** snake_case is canonical; the camelCase forms `listIds`, `scheduledTime`, `scheduledTimezone`, `mediaUrl` are also accepted.

403.description: Account has an inactive billing status

409.description: A request with this Idempotency-Key is already being processed

422.description: Validation failed, unknown list ids, or an invalid/past/too-far scheduled_time intent

value.message: list_ids must be a non-empty array of list IDs

errors.message: list_ids must be a non-empty array of list IDs

post.summary: Send a test message of a broadcast to one phone
post.description:
Sends a single test message of the broadcast's content to one phone number so you can eyeball it on a real handset before scheduling. Works on a `drafting` or `pending` broadcast.

**Read-only:** this never creates a contact and never changes the broadcast's state.

**Fidelity — a test can only approximate a real send:**
- If the phone matches an existing contact in the account, the standard merge fields (`%FIRST_NAME%`, `%LAST_NAME%`, `%EMAIL%`, `%PHONE%`, `%BIRTHDAY%`) render from that contact (`test.personalized: true`).
- Otherwise they render as human-readable placeholders like `[First name]` (`test.personalized: false`).
- Custom-field tokens are not resolved for a test and are stripped (matching a real send's empty-field behavior).
- `%SHORT_LINK(url)%` / `%SHORT_UNIQUE_LINK(url)%` mint **real, clickable tracked short links**, so you can verify the link resolves and see the true message length. They are recorded under a separate `broadcast.test` origin, so test clicks never appear in the broadcast's own link analytics. If the test phone matches no contact, a `%SHORT_UNIQUE_LINK%` falls back to a shared tracked link (a per-contact link needs a contact).
- The test is sent from the **same number the real broadcast would use** for that recipient: their existing conversation's number when they have one, otherwise the account's number for their country.

The fully rendered body is returned as `test.rendered_message`, and `test.message_type` / `test.segments_per_message` / `test.credits_per_recipient` describe that rendered body (merge fields filled, links shortened) rather than the raw template. `segments_per_message` is the real segment count; `credits_per_recipient` is what it costs. **This consumes one message's worth of credits** (it is a real send). Response is `202` (queued).

**Rate limit:** 1 request/second per credential. **Idempotency:** supports the `Idempotency-Key` header.

403.description: Account has an inactive billing status

404.description: Broadcast not found (or not in this account)

409.description: Broadcast is not in a testable (draft or pending) state

422.description: Missing/invalid test phone, or no account phone available to send from

post.summary: Schedule (confirm) a draft broadcast, or send it now
post.description:
Confirms a draft and schedules it: transitions the broadcast from `drafting` to `pending` and queues the delayed send job. Only a broadcast in `drafting` status can be scheduled (otherwise `409`).

**Timing — the request must be explicit about WHEN to send. A send time is required somewhere: this body, the draft's stored intent, or `send_now: true`.** Precedence:
1. a `scheduled_time` in this request body → schedule at that time (validated: Eastern default, explicit offset/`Z` wins, past-60s and >366-days rejected `422`);
2. otherwise, the time the draft was created with (its stored intent) → schedule then. If that stored time has already passed, the request is rejected `422` (`scheduled_time_in_past`) — supply a fresh `scheduled_time`, or `send_now: true` to send it anyway;
3. otherwise (no time anywhere) → the request is rejected `422` (`send_time_required`). Send `scheduled_time` to schedule it, or `send_now: true` to send it immediately. A confirm call that lost its body never blasts the list.

`send_now: true` short-circuits all of the above and sends immediately — it is the ONLY way to send immediately; pairing it with `scheduled_time` is rejected `422` (`send_now_conflict`).

**Credit budget is ENFORCED here** against a freshly computed estimate: if projected usage would exceed the account's remaining budget the request is rejected `422` with `error: "CREDIT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED"` and the `estimate` block, and the broadcast stays a draft.

**Accounts under broadcast review** receive `200` with `review_status: "pending"`; the broadcast is not queued and sends only after approval.

**Rate limit:** 1 request/second per credential. **Idempotency:** supports the `Idempotency-Key` header. On any handled failure the broadcast remains a recoverable draft.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Roezan broadcast ID (must currently be a draft).

200.description: Broadcast scheduled, sending now, or pending review

403.description: Account has an inactive billing status

404.description: Broadcast not found (or not in this account)

409.description: Broadcast is not a draft, or a request with this Idempotency-Key is already being processed

422.description: Missing, invalid, or stale scheduled_time, or credit limit exceeded

creditLimit.summary: Estimated credits exceed the remaining budget

value.message: Estimated credits (12000) would exceed the account's remaining credit budget (used 4000 of 10000)

stale.summary: The draft's stored time has passed

value.message: The draft's scheduled time (2026-06-01T10:00:00Z) has already passed — the current time is 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z. Provide a new scheduled_time to reschedule, or "send_now": true to send it immediately

errors.message: The draft's scheduled time (2026-06-01T10:00:00Z) has already passed — the current time is 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z. Provide a new scheduled_time to reschedule, or "send_now": true to send it immediately

noSendTime.summary: No send time anywhere — neither this body nor the draft says when

value.message: This broadcast has no scheduled time. Send "scheduled_time" to schedule it, or "send_now": true to send it immediately

errors.message: This broadcast has no scheduled time. Send "scheduled_time" to schedule it, or "send_now": true to send it immediately

500.description: Server error (the broadcast remains a draft)

post.description:
Cancels a scheduled (`pending`) broadcast: removes its delayed send job and reverts it to a `drafting` draft. Only a `pending` broadcast can be canceled (otherwise `409`). A broadcast that has already started or finished sending cannot be canceled here.

**Rate limit:** 1 request/second per credential. **Idempotency:** supports the `Idempotency-Key` header.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Roezan broadcast ID (must currently be pending).

200.description: Broadcast canceled and reverted to a draft

404.description: Broadcast not found (or not in this account)

409.description: Broadcast is not in a cancelable (pending) state

get.summary: Get a broadcast's status and delivery stats
get.description: Returns a broadcast's current status, schedule, and delivery counters, scoped to the authenticated account. Poll this after scheduling to answer "did it send?" — `status` moves `drafting` → `pending` → `in-progress` → `complete` (or `canceled`/`error`), and the delivery counters populate as the send runs.

404.description: Broadcast not found (or not in this account)

get.description: Returns the lists a contact is currently subscribed to, by Roezan contact ID.

404.description: Contact not found (or not in this account)

get.description:
Returns every webhook subscription on the account, including those created in the Roezan dashboard and by connected apps such as Zapier.

Signing secrets are never returned — `metadata.signingSecretSet` reports whether one exists.

post.description:
Registers a URL to receive an event. One subscription is one (event, URL) pair — call this once per event if you want several delivered to the same URL.

`message.status` is **early access**: subscribing to it requires the feature to be enabled for your account. Contact support to request it.

400.description: Missing/invalid event or URL, a URL that is not publicly resolvable, or an event this account is not enabled for.

post.summary: Roezan POSTs the event to your URL
post.description:
Sent as `application/json`. Your endpoint should respond 2xx promptly (we time out at 15 seconds) and do its own work asynchronously.

**Retries** — a failed delivery is retried with exponential backoff. After repeated failures the subscription is marked broken and stops receiving events until reactivated from the dashboard.

**Two status codes are meaningful:** respond `410 Gone` and we delete the subscription permanently; respond `404` and we mark it broken. Any other non-2xx is treated as a transient failure and retried.

**Signature verification** — for `message.status` and `message.receive`, when the subscription carries a signing secret, the request includes `X-Roezan-Signature: sha256=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body. Compute it over the bytes exactly as received, before any JSON parsing or re-serialisation.

**Ordering** — do not assume delivery order. Every payload carries a timestamp; order by that, not by arrival.

parameters.name: X-Roezan-Signature
parameters.description: `sha256=<hex>` HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, present only when the subscription has a signing secret.

schema.description: Shape depends on the subscribed event. The two documented here are the highest-volume; every payload carries an `event` field naming its type, and a live sample for any event is available in the Roezan dashboard when creating the webhook.

404.description: Endpoint not found — the subscription is marked broken and stops receiving events.

410.description: Gone — the subscription is deleted permanently.

default.description: Treated as a transient failure and retried with backoff.

delete.description: Stops deliveries for this subscription. Deleting is the only way to stop an event you have subscribed to.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Subscription ID returned when it was created.

phone.description:
The recipient's phone number. Send it in E.164 — `+`, country code, number, e.g. `+4522821817` — which is the only form that says which country it belongs to. Spaces, dashes and parentheses are ignored.

Digits without a `+` are assumed to be a US or Canadian number wherever they could be one. A ten-digit Danish or Norwegian number fits that shape too, so send any number outside the US and Canada with its `+`.

countryCode.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of `phone` (e.g. `IT`, `GB`). Only consulted when `phone` has no `+`: the digits are read as a number in that country, with or without its country code (`3123456789` or `393123456789` with `IT`), and the hint is ignored if they aren't a valid number there. A `+` in `phone` always wins. Sending `phone` in E.164 makes this unnecessary.

from.description:
Which of your Roezan numbers to send from, in E.164 format (`+` then country code and number — no spaces or dashes inside it; surrounding whitespace is ignored). Must be a number on your account that can send; list them with `GET /api/integrations/senders`.

Omit it (or send an empty string) to let Roezan choose: the number the contact last messaged, otherwise one that can reach the contact's country, preferring your primary number.

`from` applies to this message only. Later automatic sends to the contact still use the number they last messaged — so if they reply to this number, it becomes their number from then on.

A `from` that is malformed, not on your account, or unable to send is rejected with `422` before anything is queued. A `from` that cannot reach this particular contact (for example a US number and a UK contact) is checked when the message is processed and the message is **not sent** — Roezan never swaps in a different number than the one you asked for.

message.example: Thanks for signing up for our service!

media.description: One or more media URLs to send as MMS. A bare string is also accepted and treated as a single-item list.

mediaUrl.description: Single media URL, merged with `media` into one list. Prefer `media`; `mediaUrl` (and its `media_url` alias) is accepted for existing integrations.

phone.description: The contact's phone number in E.164 (`+`, country code, number, e.g. `+4522821817`). Digits without a `+` are assumed to be a US or Canadian number wherever they could be one. Also accepted as `phone_number` or `phoneNumber`.

firstName.description: Optional. Previously documented as required, but never enforced.

lists.description: Array of list IDs the Contact should be subscribed to. List IDs can be fetched from the `api/integrations/lists` method

tags.description: Array of tag IDs the Contact should be tagged with. Tag IDs can be fetched from the `api/integrations/tags` method

list.description: List ID. Also accepted as `lists` or `listIds`, and may be an array.

phone.description: The contact's phone number in E.164 (`+`, country code, number, e.g. `+4522821817`). Digits without a `+` are assumed to be a US or Canadian number wherever they could be one.
The contact's phone number in E.164 (`+`, country code, number, e.g. `+4522821817`). Digits without a `+` are assumed to be a US or Canadian number wherever they could be one.
The contact's phone number in E.164 (`+`, country code, number, e.g. `+4522821817`). Digits without a `+` are assumed to be a US or Canadian number wherever they could be one.

tagId.description: The Tag ID to be removed from the given Contact (found by Phone)

subscribed.description: Number of contacts added under this List (including opted-out contacts)

status.description: Delivery state in the same vocabulary as the `message.status` webhook. Outbound: `pending` (not yet handed to the carrier), `sent` (handed to the carrier; best-effort, some carriers advance straight to `delivered`), `delivered` (carrier confirmed, or the carrier never reported and the message is treated as delivered), `read` (RCS read receipt), `failed` (see `failure_reason`). Inbound messages are always `received`.

failure_reason.description: Human-readable reason when `status` is `failed` (for example a carrier filter or an invalid destination). `null` otherwise.

category.description: Stable, external-facing channel/source. Never the internal `BC_123`-style string.

media.description: MMS attachments. Empty for SMS. Each item is the media MIME type and its URL.

next_cursor.description: Opaque pagination token. Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next (older) page. Treat as opaque — do not construct or decode it. `null` on the last page.

has_more.description: True when another page is available.

next_cursor.description: Opaque pagination token. Pass back as `cursor` to fetch the next page. Treat as opaque — do not construct or decode it. `null` on the last page.

has_more.description: True when another page is available.

list_ids.description: Target list IDs (alias: `listIds`). De-duplicated; max 100. Every ID must belong to the account.

message.description: Message body. Required — a broadcast cannot be media-only. Supports the same merge fields and `%SHORT_LINK(...)%` / `%SHORT_UNIQUE_LINK(...)%` placeholders as the app.

media.description: Optional http(s) media URLs sent as MMS (max 10). A bare string is accepted, as are the single-URL aliases `media_url` / `mediaUrl`. Each URL must end in a recognized file extension.

scheduled_time.description:
Intended send time, STORED (not scheduled) on the draft (alias: `scheduledTime`). Validated now; confirm it with a bare `/schedule` call, or override it there. Omitting it here means `/schedule` must supply a `scheduled_time` or `send_now: true`.

**Accepted formats (anything else is rejected `422` `scheduled_time_invalid` — no best-effort parsing):**
- `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` — e.g. `2026-08-01 10:00`
- `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` — e.g. `2026-08-01 10:00:30`
- the same two with a `T` separator, optionally with `.SSS` milliseconds
- `YYYY-MM-DD` alone — midnight in the applied timezone
- any of the above with a trailing `Z`, `+HH:mm`/`-HH:mm`, or `+HHmm`/`-HHmm`

Formats like `08/01/2026 10:00`, `Aug 1 2026`, RFC 2822, and epoch milliseconds are **rejected**, not guessed: they parse against the host's timezone rather than yours and would silently schedule the send hours off.

A value with an explicit offset or `Z` is an absolute instant and `scheduled_timezone` is ignored. Everything else is wall-clock time in `scheduled_timezone` (Eastern by default).

scheduled_timezone.description: IANA timezone applied to `scheduled_time` (alias: `scheduledTimezone`). Defaults to America/New_York. Rejected if provided without `scheduled_time`.

ScheduleBroadcast.description: Body for POST /broadcasts/{id}/schedule. Every field is individually optional, but the request must say WHEN to send: omitting `scheduled_time` when the draft has no stored intent either is rejected `422` (`send_time_required`) rather than sent. `send_now: true` is REQUIRED to send immediately — it is the only input that produces an immediate send, whatever the draft stored.

scheduled_time.description:
When to send (alias: `scheduledTime`). Overrides the draft's stored intent. Omit to fall back to the stored intent; if the draft has none, the request is rejected `422` (`send_time_required`) — pass `send_now: true` instead to send immediately.

**Accepted formats (anything else is rejected `422` `scheduled_time_invalid`):** `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm[:ss]`, the same with a `T` separator and optional `.SSS`, `YYYY-MM-DD` alone (midnight in the applied timezone), each optionally suffixed with `Z`, `+HH:mm`/`-HH:mm`, or `+HHmm`/`-HHmm`. Formats such as `08/01/2026 10:00`, `Aug 1 2026`, RFC 2822, and epoch milliseconds are rejected rather than guessed — they would parse against the host timezone and schedule the send hours off.

Explicit offset/`Z` wins over `scheduled_timezone`.

scheduled_timezone.description: IANA timezone applied to `scheduled_time` (alias: `scheduledTimezone`). Defaults to America/New_York.

send_now.description: Send immediately, ignoring any time stored on the draft (alias: `sendNow`). REQUIRED for an immediate send — no other input sends now, so a request that loses its body is rejected rather than blasting the list (`422` `send_time_required`). It is also the only way to confirm a draft whose stored `scheduled_time` has already passed — omitting the time falls back to that stale value, which is rejected `422` `scheduled_time_in_past`. Combining `send_now` with `scheduled_time` is rejected `422` `send_now_conflict`.

phone.description: The single phone number to send the test message to (aliases: `phone_number`, `phoneNumber`).

message_type.description: Classification of `rendered_message` (the body actually sent), not of the raw template.

segments_per_message.description: Real text-segment count of `rendered_message`. **Not a cost multiplier** — an MMS is one segment but costs more than one credit. Use `credits_per_recipient` for cost.

credits_per_recipient.description: Credits this message costs per recipient. An MMS (media attached, or a body spanning three or more segments) costs 3 regardless of its real segment count; a plain SMS costs one credit per segment.

rendered_message.description: The exact body sent to the test phone, after merge fields are filled and short-link tokens are replaced with real tracked links.
rendered_message.example: Hi Satoshi, our sale starts today! Shop https://rzn.co/Ab3dEf9xQ1

personalized.description: True when the phone matched an existing contact and merge fields rendered from it; false when placeholders were used.

message.example: Test message queued (personalized from the matching contact)

recipients.description: De-duplicated deliverable recipient count across the target lists (excludes unsubscribed/opted-out/invalid/deleted).

segments_per_message.description: Real text-segment count of the message body. **Not a cost multiplier** — an MMS is one segment but costs more than one credit. Use `credits_per_recipient` for cost.

credits_per_recipient.description: Credits each recipient costs. An MMS (media attached, or a body spanning three or more segments) costs 3 regardless of its real segment count; a plain SMS costs one credit per segment.

estimated_credits.description: recipients × credits_per_recipient. This is the figure the credit budget is checked against and the amount actually charged.

credit_limit.description: Projected usage ceiling before an upgrade is required (2 × (plan + rollover credits)).

within_budget.description: False when estimated usage would exceed the remaining budget. Informational at create; enforced at `/schedule`.

status.description: `drafting` for a freshly created draft; `pending` once scheduled.

review_status.description: `pending` when the account is under broadcast review; otherwise null.

segments_per_message.description: Real text-segment count of the stored message body. **Not a cost multiplier** — a broadcast can report `message_type: "MMS"` and `segments_per_message: 1` at the same time, because attaching media makes it an MMS without adding a segment. Use `credits_per_recipient` for cost.

credits_per_recipient.description: Credits each recipient costs, as quoted when the broadcast was created. An MMS (media attached, or a body spanning three or more segments) costs 3 regardless of its real segment count; a plain SMS costs one credit per segment.

scheduled_time.description: Echo of the requested wall-clock time; null for drafts.

scheduled_timezone.description: Timezone applied; null for drafts or offset-bearing input.

scheduled_at_utc.description: Resolved intended send instant in UTC; null when no time was given.

delivery_schedule.description: Stored naive scheduled datetime (server time); null when no time was given.

BroadcastScheduled.description: Response for /schedule and /cancel: the broadcast in its new state, plus (for /schedule) the enforced estimate.

immediate.description: True when the broadcast was sent immediately (`send_now: true`). Present on the /schedule response.

recipient_count.description: Recipients the broadcast was actually sent to (populated as/after the send runs).

opted_in.description: 1 when the contact is opted in to messaging, 0 otherwise.

safe_sending_start_hour.description: Local hour (0-23) before which messaging is suppressed.

safe_sending_end_hour.description: Local hour (0-23) after which messaging is suppressed.

fullName.description: Convenience concatenation of first and last name.

MessageReceiveWebhook.description: Payload POSTed to a subscribed account webhook when a contact sends an inbound message (event `message.receive`). `to` (and `recipient`) say which of your numbers received it. When a signing secret is configured, the request carries `X-Roezan-Signature: sha256=<hex>` — an HMAC-SHA256 of the exact raw request body.

contactId.description: Roezan contact ID of the sender.

converseUrl.description: Deep link to the conversation in the Roezan admin.

received.description: When the message was received (ISO-8601 with offset).

type.description: `mms` when the message carries media, `rcs` when it arrived on an RCS agent, otherwise `sms` — the same values as `type` on `message.status`. (Before API 1.9.0 this was always `sms`.)

from.description: The contact's number — who sent the message — in E.164.

to.description: Your Roezan number the message was sent to, in E.164. Use it to tell your numbers apart. A single value, not a list: Roezan conversations are one contact to one of your numbers. Null when the message arrived on a sender that is not a phone number (an RCS agent — see `recipient`), or if the number could not be resolved.

recipient.description: Your Roezan sender the message arrived on. Null if it could not be resolved.

MessageStatusWebhook.description: Payload POSTed to a subscribed account webhook when delivery statuses of outbound messages change (event `message.status`). EARLY ACCESS: creating a hook for this event requires the feature to be enabled for your account — contact support. ALWAYS a batch envelope: `events` carries 1 to 250 entries per request, ordered by `occurredAt` — iterate the array and never assume a single entry. Broadcast- and reminder-origin statuses are only delivered to hooks that opted in via `includeBroadcasts`. When a signing secret is configured, the request carries `X-Roezan-Signature: sha256=<hex>` — an HMAC-SHA256 of the exact raw request body.

events.description: One entry per message status change, ordered by `occurredAt` ascending.

MessageStatusWebhookEvent.description: One outbound message's status change, as carried in the `events` array of a `message.status` webhook.

messageId.description: Roezan message ID — matches the `id` returned by the message history API.

status.description: New external status. `delivered`, `read`, and `failed` are dependable; `sent` is best-effort and carrier-dependent. `failed` is ALMOST always terminal, but a late carrier receipt may rarely supersede it with a `delivered` for the same `messageId` — treat the later event (by `occurredAt`) as authoritative.

previousStatus.description: Prior external status, or null when the message had no externally visible status yet.

origin.description: What kind of send produced the message. `broadcast` and `reminder` statuses require the hook's `includeBroadcasts` opt-in.

contact.description: RECIPIENT contact snapshot (camelCase). Null when the contact no longer exists.

phoneNumber.description: Country code + national digits, no leading +.

phoneNumberE164.description: E.164 form with leading +; null when unparseable.

sender.description: Sender identity the message went out on ("which of my numbers sent this"). Null when unresolved.

errorCode.description: Carrier error code as a string; only set when `status` is `failed`.

failureReason.description: Human-readable failure classification derived from `errorCode`; only set when `status` is `failed`.

occurredAt.description: When the status changed (ISO-8601 with offset). Order entries by this field.

from.description: Your Roezan number the message was sent from, in E.164 (the same as `sender.numberE164`). Null when the sender is not a phone number.

to.description: The contact's number, in E.164 (the same as `contact.phoneNumberE164`).

WebhookContact.description: Contact snapshot embedded in outbound webhook payloads.

opted_in.description: 1 when the contact is opted in to messaging, 0 otherwise.

tags.description: Tags currently applied to the contact.

lists.description: Lists the contact is currently subscribed to (`subscribed = 1`). Unsubscribed memberships are retained as history but are not included here.

event.description: The event to subscribe to. `message.status` is early access — contact support to enable it for your account.

hookUrl.description: HTTPS URL we POST to when the event fires. Must be publicly resolvable; private/internal addresses are rejected. Aliases `target_url`, `url`, and `targetUrl` are also accepted.

name.description: Label shown in the Roezan dashboard. Defaults to an auto-generated name.

lists.description: Optional. Restrict deliveries to contacts subscribed to these list IDs. Honoured by `message.receive` and `message.status`.

tags.description: Optional. Restrict `tag.added` / `tag.removed` deliveries to these tag IDs.

includeBroadcasts.description: `message.status` only. Off by default. When enabled, statuses from broadcasts and event reminders are delivered as well as 1:1 conversation traffic. These are per-recipient — one broadcast can produce thousands of events (batched up to 250 per request) — which is why they are a separate opt-in. Must be a real boolean; the string "false" is treated as false.

signingSecret.description: `message.status` and `message.receive`. When set, every delivery of those events carries an `X-Roezan-Signature` header so you can verify the request came from Roezan. Never returned by the API once stored — send an empty string to remove it.

WebhookSubscription.description: A stored webhook subscription. One row per (event, URL) pair — subscribe again to register a second event against the same URL.

broken.description: Set when deliveries have failed repeatedly, or the endpoint returned 404. A broken subscription receives nothing until it is reactivated from the Roezan dashboard.

metadata.description: Stored options. `signingSecretSet` reports whether a signing secret exists; the secret itself is never returned.

code.description: Why the request was rejected: `from_invalid` — not E.164; `from_not_found` — not a number on your account; `from_not_sendable` — on your account but unable to send (see `reason`); `idempotency_key_reused` — the `Idempotency-Key` was already used for a request with a different body. Absent on the missing-field rejections.

reason.description: For `from_not_sendable`: `RELEASED`, `HIDDEN` (held in reserve), `TFV_PENDING` (toll-free verification not yet approved), `TFV_REJECTED`, or `SENDER_INACTIVE`. Null otherwise.

message.example: Pending A2P verification approval — this number can't send until it's approved

WebhookSender.description: One of your Roezan senders. `id` is stable and is the same across `GET /api/integrations/senders`, `sender` on `message.status` and `recipient` on `message.receive`.

channel.description: `sms` for phone numbers; `rcs` for RCS agents.

number.description: Country code + number, no leading `+`. Null for senders that are not phone numbers.

label.description: The name you gave the number in Roezan.

canSend.description: Whether `from` can name this number right now.

reason.description: Why `canSend` is false — the same values as `reason` on a `from_not_sendable` rejection.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional. A unique client-generated key that makes retries safe: the first request with a given key runs and its response is cached for 24 hours; identical retries replay that response verbatim with an `Idempotency-Replayed: true` response header; a duplicate arriving while the first is still in flight returns `409`; reusing a key for a request with a different body (or a different resource in the path) returns `422` with `code: "idempotency_key_reused"` rather than replaying the other request's response. Scoped per account + endpoint. Recommended for AI-harness/automation callers that may retry on network errors. 5xx responses are not cached (retry proceeds). **A key names one request, not one attempt at it:** if a request was rejected `422` because of its body (e.g. `from_invalid`, a missing `phone`), that rejection is what the key now replays — correct the body and send it under a NEW key, or the corrected request is refused with `idempotency_key_reused`. Rejections that depend on account state rather than the body (`from_not_found`, `from_not_sendable`) are not cached, so a retry under the same key is judged afresh.
